name: medical_phi_replay
description: Sanitised clinical PHI replay corpus — 30 synthetic cases across four sub-domains (primary care, radiology, oncology, mental health) plus 2 cross-domain edge cases. 15 cases cover the bundled medical-regex baseline (icd_code with clinical context, six-drug-list medication-dosage, lab_value with clinical context, diagnosis_text prefix). 15 cases marked known_gap: true exercise coverage gaps that require an adapter-side medical NER model — drug names without dosage, drugs outside the six-drug list, free-text symptom narratives, procedure mentions, condition narratives in RAG context, TNM staging, chemotherapy regimens, targeted-therapy mentions, imaging-finding free text, CPT procedure codes, and suicidality narratives. All patient identifiers and clinical narratives are synthetic — no real patient data. Public clinical references (ICD codes, lab marker names, generic drug names, CPT codes) are kept literal because the regex shapes depend on them; those are public diagnostic / pharmaceutical / billing identifiers, not PHI. Companion artifact for docs/medical-ner-adapter-recipe.md — operators wiring a medical-NER detector via register_detector_family() can use this corpus as a baseline-versus-known-gap regression target across multiple clinical sub-specialties before measuring against their own internal validation set.

message.content: Latest patient note: diagnosis includes E11.9 with associated retinopathy follow-up scheduled for next month.

cases.notes: ICD-10 code (type 2 diabetes mellitus without complications) caught by medical-regex's icd_code pattern. ICD codes themselves are public diagnostic identifiers; the PHI character comes from associating them with a patient context, which the firewall redacts to keep clinical-narrative outputs safe.

message.content: Per the patient's latest history, HbA1c: 8.4% and creatinine: 1.2 mg/dL — recommend follow-up at the next clinical visit.

cases.notes: Two lab-value matches in one payload (HbA1c, creatinine) — medical-regex's lab_value pattern requires a clinical-context anchor (patient/clinical/history/...) within 60 chars. Lab marker names are public; the PHI shape is the patient-specific number-and-unit pairing in a clinical narrative.

message.content: Per the chart, the patient was started on metformin 500 mg twice daily and lisinopril 10 mg in the morning.

cases.notes: Two medication-dosage matches from the bundled six-drug list (metformin + lisinopril). medical-regex's medication_dosage pattern requires both a known drug name and a numeric dosage; either alone won't fire.

message.content: Summary: Diagnosis: hypertension, stage 2 with mild proteinuria. Patient referred to nephrology consult.

cases.notes: diagnosis_text pattern fires on the 'Diagnosis: <free-text>' shape and captures the diagnosis string as the redactable group. Note: Stage descriptors and chronic-condition names are not themselves PHI; the redaction is conservative because the pattern fires whenever a model emits diagnosis-prefixed clinical content.

rag_context: Retrieved note 003: Patient diagnosis E11.65 (type 2 diabetes with hyperglycemia) with HbA1c: 9.1% and active medication list includes insulin 24 units before bed.

cases.notes: Three medical-regex hits in a single RAG-context surface — the input gate of the healthcare profile tokenises PHI before it reaches the model, so the redacted RAG context is what the LLM sees. Validates surface-level coverage on input.rag_context, not just output.content.

message.content: Per the visit note, the patient discontinued gabapentin yesterday after three weeks on the medication.

cases.notes: medical-regex's medication_dosage pattern requires both a drug name AND a numeric dosage. Bare medication names without dosages are silently passed through. A medical NER adapter (med7, MedSpaCy, Medical-BERT) recognises drug names independently of dosage and is the intended path for catching this shape — see docs/medical-ner-adapter-recipe.md.

message.content: The patient was started on semaglutide 0.5 mg weekly per the endocrinology consult.

cases.notes: medical-regex's medication_dosage pattern hardcodes a six-drug list (metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, insulin, warfarin, albuterol). Dosage-format drugs outside that list — semaglutide here, but also any GLP-1, SGLT-2, biologic, or chemotherapy agent — are not detected. A medical NER adapter is required for general drug-name coverage.

message.content: Pt reports persistent nausea, intermittent chest pain since last Tuesday, and increased fatigue over the past week — recommend ECG and basic metabolic panel.

cases.notes: Free-text symptom narratives are not pattern-matchable — there is no closed-set vocabulary the regex layer can enumerate. A medical NER model trained on clinical notes can extract symptom mentions; the regex layer cannot. Clinical free-text is the largest medical-regex coverage gap.

message.content: The patient underwent percutaneous coronary intervention last week and is recovering well in the cardiac step-down unit.

cases.notes: Procedure mentions follow no fixed pattern that the regex layer can match. A clinical NER model with a PROCEDURE label can flag these; medical-regex passes them through. CPT/HCPCS code shapes (numeric procedure codes) might be a separate regex extension; free-text procedure names need NER.

rag_context: Retrieved note 005: The patient's congestive heart failure exacerbation responded well to diuretics, pulmonary edema cleared on follow-up imaging, and exercise tolerance is improving.

cases.notes: Chronic condition mentions in RAG-context narratives — analogous to the symptom case but on the input side. A medical NER adapter on input.rag_context tokenises these before the LLM sees them; medical-regex passes them through, leaving the model to ingest unredacted condition references.

message.content: Patient with acute dyspnea: CT pulmonary angiogram confirms I26.99 with bilateral segmental filling defects in the lower lobes.

cases.notes: Radiology dictation referencing a pulmonary embolism ICD-10 code (I26.99) with patient-anchored clinical context. icd_code regex fires; the imaging-finding free text around it is not separately matched (that is the gap exercised in rad-ner-required-imaging-finding).

message.content: Per the patient's pre-imaging workup, creatinine: 1.4 mg/dL — within acceptable range for iodinated contrast administration during the CT abdomen study.

cases.notes: Renal-function check is standard before contrast-enhanced radiology studies. lab_value regex fires on creatinine in patient-anchored context. The surrounding 'iodinated contrast' / 'CT abdomen' phrasing is uncaught radiology terminology — not included in sensitive_values because it is not the PHI shape this case is testing.

message.content: Impression: Diagnosis: acute pulmonary embolism, right lower lobe segmental branches. Recommend anticoagulation initiation.

sensitive_values: acute pulmonary embolism, right lower lobe segmental branches
expected_absent: acute pulmonary embolism, right lower lobe segmental branches
cases.notes: Diagnosis-prefix dictation from a radiology report. diagnosis_text fires on the 'Diagnosis: <free-text>' shape independent of clinical-context anchors and captures up to the first period or 80-char limit.

message.content: Pt CT chest demonstrates a 3.2 cm spiculated mass in the right upper lobe with associated mediastinal lymphadenopathy and a small pleural effusion.

cases.notes: Imaging-finding free text does not match any bundled regex — measurements with 'cm', anatomical descriptors, and lesion-characterisation language need an NER model trained on radiology dictation. RadBERT and similar imaging-tuned models target exactly this shape; the bundled regex layer passes it through verbatim.

message.content: Patient imaging order: 70551 followed by 71250 for the same encounter; clinical indication is documented in the chart.

cases.notes: CPT codes are 5-digit numerics (70551 = MRI brain w/o contrast; 71250 = CT chest w/o contrast). The bundled icd_code regex requires a leading [A-TV-Z] letter and explicitly excludes plain 5-digit numbers. The bundled detectors do not provide CPT/HCPCS code coverage; these cases remain known gaps. Note: 5-digit numbers are also the shape of US ZIP codes — adding a CPT regex without a clinical-context anchor would produce significant FPs.

rag_context: Retrieved imaging note 027: Pt completed MRI brain with gadolinium last month, followed by repeat MRI lumbar spine without contrast this week to evaluate disc herniation progression.

cases.notes: Imaging-modality narrative in RAG context. Modality terms (MRI, CT, PET, ultrasound) and contrast-protocol descriptors are not in any closed-set vocabulary the regex layer matches. A medical-NER adapter on input.rag_context with PROCEDURE / MODALITY labels is the catch path.

message.content: Patient diagnosis C50.911 confirmed on biopsy; oncology team to coordinate neoadjuvant treatment planning at next clinical visit.

cases.notes: Malignancy ICD-10 (C50.911 = malignant neoplasm of unspecified site of right female breast) with patient-anchored clinical context. icd_code fires; the 'biopsy' / 'neoadjuvant' oncology terms are uncaught domain language exercised in onc-ner-required-* cases.

message.content: Per the patient's anticoagulation history, warfarin 5 mg daily was initiated for cancer-associated venous thromboembolism prophylaxis.

cases.notes: Cancer-associated thrombosis is a common indication for warfarin in oncology. medication_dosage fires (warfarin is in the six-drug list, dosage present, patient/history context within 60 chars).

message.content: Pt summary: Diagnosis: stage IIIA non-small cell lung cancer, adenocarcinoma subtype. Multidisciplinary tumor board pending.

sensitive_values: stage IIIA non-small cell lung cancer, adenocarcinoma subtype
expected_absent: stage IIIA non-small cell lung cancer, adenocarcinoma subtype
cases.notes: Stage-and-subtype text after a 'Diagnosis:' prefix. diagnosis_text captures up to the period. The capture group is bounded by [A-Za-z0-9 ,/-] characters; the comma before 'adenocarcinoma' is preserved by the char class.

message.content: Pathology stage: T2N1M0 with extracapsular extension; recommend adjuvant chemotherapy and consideration of regional radiation.

cases.notes: TNM cancer-staging notation (Tumor / Node / Metastasis) does not match the icd_code shape — `T2N` fails the [A-TV-Z][0-9][0-9AB] requirement (`N` is not in [0-9AB]). A medical-NER model with a STAGING label is the intended catch path.

message.content: Pt is on FOLFOX cycle 3 of 12, tolerating treatment with grade 1 peripheral neuropathy and stable performance status.

cases.notes: Chemotherapy regimen acronyms (FOLFOX, R-CHOP, ABVD, AC-T) and toxicity grade language are domain-specific oncology vocabulary not enumerable in regex. A medical-NER adapter trained on oncology notes flags these via REGIMEN / TOXICITY labels.

rag_context: Retrieved oncology note 089: Pt was started on pembrolizumab Q3W per immunotherapy protocol; second-line addition of trastuzumab deruxtecan considered if HER2 status confirms.

cases.notes: Targeted-therapy and biologic drug names (checkpoint inhibitors, antibody-drug conjugates) are absent from the six-drug medication_dosage list. Frequency dosing language ('Q3W' = every 3 weeks) and biomarker references ('HER2 status') are also uncaught. NER adapter handles drug-name extraction independent of dosage; biomarker labels need a clinical-trial-aware model.

message.content: Patient diagnosis F33.1 with current major depressive episode, moderate severity; treatment plan continued with weekly therapy and medication review.

cases.notes: Mental-health ICD-10 F-code (F33.1 = recurrent major depressive disorder, moderate) with patient-anchored clinical context. icd_code fires. The 'major depressive episode' free text is not separately captured; that gap is exercised in mh-ner-required-condition-rag.

message.content: Assessment summary: Diagnosis: generalized anxiety disorder, moderate severity with secondary insomnia. Recommend cognitive behavioral therapy referral.

sensitive_values: generalized anxiety disorder, moderate severity with secondary insomnia
expected_absent: generalized anxiety disorder, moderate severity with secondary insomnia
cases.notes: Diagnosis-prefix free text in a psychiatric assessment. diagnosis_text captures up to the period or 80-char limit. Note: the trailing CBT-referral language in this case is not captured by the regex; it falls outside the diagnosis_text capture window.

message.content: Per the patient's pre-treatment history, creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL noted prior to initiating lithium therapy for bipolar disorder.

cases.notes: Renal-function baseline is standard before initiating lithium (renally cleared, narrow therapeutic index). lab_value regex fires on creatinine with patient-anchored context. The 'lithium therapy' / 'bipolar disorder' phrasing is uncaught psychiatry vocabulary — exercised in mh-ner-required-psych-medication.

message.content: Per the visit note, the patient was started on sertraline 50 mg daily and clonazepam 0.5 mg as needed for breakthrough anxiety.

cases.notes: SSRIs (sertraline, fluoxetine, escitalopram), SNRIs, benzodiazepines (clonazepam, lorazepam, alprazolam), and mood stabilisers (lithium, lamotrigine, valproate) are absent from the six-drug medication_dosage list. Psychiatric medication coverage is the largest mental-health gap and a primary driver for adopting an NER adapter in mental-health deployments.

message.content: Pt reports passive suicidal ideation without active plan or intent over the past two weeks; no prior suicide attempts; safety plan reviewed and family contacts updated.

cases.notes: Suicidality, self-harm, and safety-plan narratives are sensitive psychiatric content with no closed-set regex shape. An NER model trained on psychiatric notes (or a specialised risk-assessment classifier) flags these via SI / SAFETY-PLAN / RISK labels. Particularly important in mental-health deployments because passive disclosure of SI through model output can both leak PHI and create downstream duty-to-warn implications.

rag_context: Retrieved psych note 014: Pt's post-traumatic stress disorder with comorbid major depressive disorder has shown partial response to combined pharmacotherapy and trauma-focused cognitive behavioral therapy over the last six months.

cases.notes: Psychiatric condition narratives and therapy-modality references in RAG context. Free-text mentions of PTSD, MDD, bipolar disorder, BPD, OCD, and the corresponding therapy modalities (CBT, DBT, EMDR, IFS) require an NER model with PSYCHIATRIC-CONDITION / THERAPY labels.

rag_context: Retrieved chart 042: Patient with C50.911 on warfarin 2.5 mg daily; clinical creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL stable pre-chemo.

cases.notes: Three medical-regex pattern hits (icd_code + medication_dosage + lab_value) in a single RAG-context surface spanning oncology + anticoagulation + renal monitoring. Validates that all three pattern families fire concurrently when their respective context anchors are within the 60-char window.

message.content: Pt presents to oncology clinic with worsening anxiety and insomnia since chemotherapy initiation; recommend psychiatric referral and consideration of trazodone for sleep.

cases.notes: Cross-domain symptom narrative spanning oncology and mental-health. Captures a realistic clinical handoff shape: psychiatric symptoms emerging during cancer treatment, with a non-six-drug-list medication recommendation (trazodone). Single-domain NER adapters typically miss at least one of the three sensitive segments; a multi-domain or general-purpose clinical-NER model is needed for full coverage.
